questions.text_english: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?

options.A: t½ बनाम [R]₀ — रेखीय बढ़ता हुआ ग्राफ
options.C: वेग बनाम सांद्रता — क्षैतिज सीधी रेखा
options.D: वेग बनाम सांद्रता — घटता हुआ वक्र

options_english.C: Rate vs Concentration — horizontal straight line

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. For a first order reaction, the half-life t½ = 0.693/k, which is independent of the initial concentration [R]₀. Therefore, the graph of t½ versus [R]₀ is a horizontal straight line — a constant value regardless of concentration. Option (A) shows t½ increasing with [R]₀, which corresponds to a zero-order reaction. Option (C) shows rate independent of concentration, which is zero-order. Option (D) shows rate decreasing with concentration, which does not represent a standard simple order reaction correctly.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित विलयनों में से किसका पानी में हिमांक न्यूनतम होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water ?
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The depression in freezing point is a colligative property that depends on the total number of solute particles. CaCl₂ dissociates into 3 ions (Ca²⁺ + 2Cl⁻), giving i = 3, so the effective molality = 0.1 × 3 = 0.3 m. KCl gives i = 2 (effective 0.2 m). Glucose and urea are non-electrolytes with i = 1 (effective 0.1 m each). Since CaCl₂ produces the maximum number of particles, it causes the greatest depression in freezing point, giving the lowest freezing point.

questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a transition metal ?
questions.solution: Option (B) Ag is correct. A transition metal is defined as an element that has an incompletely filled d-subshell in its ground state or in any of its common oxidation states. Ag (Z=47) has the ground state configuration [Kr]4d¹⁰5s¹, and in its most common oxidation state Ag⁺ it has a completely filled 4d¹⁰ configuration with no unpaired d-electrons. Therefore, Ag does not strictly qualify as a transition metal by the IUPAC definition. Sc, Cu, and Hg, though having filled or half-filled d-orbitals in some states, are considered transition metals in most contexts, whereas Ag is the exception here.

questions.text_english: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than Eₐ ?
questions.solution: Option (B) e^(−Eₐ/RT) is correct. According to the Arrhenius theory and Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, the fraction of molecules possessing energy equal to or greater than the activation energy Eₐ is given by the exponential factor e^(−Eₐ/RT). This term appears in the Arrhenius equation k = Ae^(−Eₐ/RT) and represents the probability of a molecule having sufficient energy to react. Options (A) and (C) are not exponential terms and cannot represent a fraction of molecules. Option (D) e^(+Eₐ/RT) would give a value greater than 1, which cannot represent a fraction.

questions.text_english: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of CuCl₂ by using platinum electrodes ?

options.B: कैथोड पर H₂ गैस निर्मुक्त होगी।
options.C: ऐनोड पर O₂ गैस निर्मुक्त होगी।
options.D: ऐनोड पर Cl₂ गैस निर्मुक्त होगी।

options_english.B: H₂ gas will be released at cathode
options_english.C: O₂ gas will be released at anode
options_english.D: Cl₂ gas will be released at anode

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. During electrolysis of aqueous CuCl₂ with platinum electrodes, Cu²⁺ ions are preferentially reduced at the cathode (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu), since Cu²⁺ has a higher reduction potential than H⁺. At the anode, Cl⁻ ions are preferentially oxidised over water because the concentration of Cl⁻ is high and the overpotential for Cl₂ evolution is lower in concentrated solution, giving Cl₂ gas (2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻). Therefore, Cu deposits at cathode and Cl₂ is released at anode. Option (A) is wrong as Cu deposits at cathode; (B) is wrong as Cu²⁺ is preferentially reduced; (C) would occur in dilute solution.

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The secondary valency (coordination number) of the central metal ion in a complex refers to the total number of ligands coordinated to it. In [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]²⁺, there are five NH₃ ligands and one NO₂⁻ ligand directly bonded to Co, giving a total of 6 donor atoms coordinated to Co. Therefore, the secondary valency (coordination number) of Co is 6. The primary valency (oxidation state) of Co here is +3, not to be confused with secondary valency.

questions.text_english: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. HNO₃ to yield
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The –OH group in phenol is an ortho/para director and a ring activator. When phenol reacts with dilute HNO₃ at low temperature, electrophilic nitration occurs preferentially at both the ortho and para positions, giving a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol. At low temperature, only mononitration occurs, so 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) is not formed — concentrated HNO₃ with H₂SO₄ would be required for that. questions.text_english: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers ?

options.A: उनकी रासायनिक अभिक्रियाशीलता समान होती है।
options.B: उनका विशिष्ट घूर्णन समान होता है।
options.C: उनके गलनांक और क्वथनांक समान होते हैं।

options_english.A: They have the same chemical reactivity.
options_english.B: They have the same specific rotation.
options_english.C: They have the same melting or boiling point.
options_english.D: They have the same refractive index.

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct — it is NOT true about enantiomers. Enantiomers rotate plane-polarised light by equal magnitudes but in opposite directions; one rotates it clockwise (+) and the other anticlockwise (–). Therefore, their specific rotations are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, meaning they do NOT have the same specific rotation. All other statements are true: enantiomers have the same chemical reactivity (in achiral environments), the same melting and boiling points, and the same refractive index, because all other physical properties are identical for mirror-image isomers.

questions.text: ऐनिलीन सीधे नाइट्रोकरण से देता है
questions.text_english: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. The –NH₂ group in aniline is a strong ortho/para director. When aniline is directly nitrated with a nitrating mixture (HNO₃ + H₂SO₄), the amine group gets partially protonated in the acidic medium forming –NH₃⁺ which is a meta director, but the free aniline still directs to ortho and para. The net result is predominantly ortho and para products. The distribution obtained is approximately 51% ortho, 47% para, and only 2% meta. The predominance of ortho over para is due to steric effects being less significant than electronic activation at ortho position.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ऐमीनों में से किसका pKb मान न्यूनतम है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following amines has lowest pKb value ?
questions.image_description: Option (D) shows the structure of p-nitroaniline: a benzene ring with NO₂ group at para position and NH₂ group.
questions.solution: Option (A) C₆H₅–N(CH₃)₂ (N,N-dimethylaniline) is correct. A lower pKb means a stronger base (higher Kb). Among aromatic amines, the basicity increases with electron-donating groups on nitrogen. N,N-dimethylaniline has two methyl groups on nitrogen which donate electrons inductively, making the nitrogen lone pair more available for protonation compared to N-methylaniline or aniline. p-nitroaniline (D) is the weakest base because the strongly electron-withdrawing –NO₂ group withdraws electron density from the ring and nitrogen via resonance, greatly reducing basicity (highest pKb). Therefore, N,N-dimethylaniline has the lowest pKb (strongest base) among the given options.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित विटामिनों में से किसकी हीनता से RBC की भुरभुरेपन में वृद्धि तथा मांसपेशियों की कमज़ोरी हो जाती है ?
questions.text_english: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness ?
questions.solution: Option (C) Vitamin E is correct. Vitamin E (tocopherol) is a fat-soluble vitamin that acts as an antioxidant, protecting cell membranes including red blood cells from oxidative damage. Its deficiency leads to increased fragility of RBCs (haemolytic anaemia) and muscular weakness (myopathy). Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness. Vitamin K deficiency leads to impaired blood clotting. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. Therefore, Vitamin E is specifically associated with RBC fragility and muscular weakness.

questions.text_english: What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason. What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?

key_points: Phenol and aniline show negative deviation from Raoult's law.

Reason: Phenol (–OH) and aniline (–NH₂) form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with each other, which are stronger than the interactions in the pure components (phenol–phenol and aniline–aniline H-bonds). This extra attraction reduces the tendency of molecules to escape into vapour phase, lowering the vapour pressure below the ideal value.
Boiling point increases above the ideal value because negative deviation means lower vapour pressure, requiring a higher temperature to boil.

questions.solution: The mixture of phenol and aniline shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. Phenol contains a highly polar –OH group and aniline contains a –NH₂ group; when mixed, phenol molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with aniline molecules (O–H···N type). These new A–B interactions are stronger than the original A–A (phenol–phenol) and B–B (aniline–aniline) interactions. As a result, the escaping tendency of molecules decreases, so the vapour pressure of the mixture is less than the ideal value predicted by Raoult's law — hence negative deviation. Since the vapour pressure is lower than expected, a higher temperature is needed to make the vapour pressure equal to atmospheric pressure; therefore, the boiling point of the mixture increases above the values expected ideally.

questions.text_english: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.

key_points: Resonance / partial double bond character: The lone pair of electrons on the halogen atom in haloarenes is delocalized into the aromatic ring by resonance, giving the C–X bond partial double bond character. This makes the bond stronger and shorter than in haloalkanes, making it difficult for a nucleophile to attack and break the bond.

sp² carbon: In haloarenes, the carbon bearing the halogen is sp² hybridized. The sp² carbon is more electronegative than sp³ carbon, so it holds the bonding electrons more tightly, making nucleophilic attack difficult. In haloalkanes, the carbon is sp³ hybridized, which is more susceptible to nucleophilic attack.

questions.solution: Haloarenes are less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution for two main reasons. First, in haloarenes the lone pair of electrons on the halogen atom is in conjugation with the pi electrons of the benzene ring through resonance. This gives the C–X bond a partial double bond character, making it shorter and stronger than a normal C–X single bond. This extra bond strength makes it difficult for a nucleophile to break the bond. Second, the carbon atom bearing the halogen in a haloarene is sp² hybridized. Since sp² carbons are more electronegative than sp³ carbons, the C–X bond electrons are held more tightly, reducing the susceptibility of the carbon to nucleophilic attack. Both factors together make haloarenes far less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution.

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: (a) निम्नलिखित उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के IUPAC नाम लिखिए : (i) [Ag(NH₃)₂][Ag(CN)₂]   (ii) K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃]
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds : (i) [Ag(NH₃)₂][Ag(CN)₂]   (ii) K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃]

key_points: (i) Diamminesilver(I) dicyanoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

sub_questions.solution: For (i) [Ag(NH₃)₂][Ag(CN)₂]: The cation [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ has Ag in +1 oxidation state with two ammonia (ammine) ligands — named diamminesilver(I). The anion [Ag(CN)₂]⁻ has Ag in +1 state with two cyanide (cyano) ligands — named dicyanoargentate(I). Full IUPAC name: Diamminesilver(I) dicyanoargentate(I). For (ii) K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃]: Potassium is the counter cation. In the complex anion, Fe is in +3 oxidation state (since 3 oxalate ions each carry 2– charge give 6–, and K₃ gives 3+ outside, so Fe = +3). Three oxalate (C₂O₄²⁻) ligands are named trioxalato. Full IUPAC name: Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III).

sub_questions.text: (b) (i) यह दर्शने के लिए कि [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl और [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ आयनन समावयव हैं, एक रासायनिक परीक्षण दीजिए। (ii) 'कीलेट प्रभाव' से क्या अभिप्राय है ? एक उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) (i) Give a chemical test to show that [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl and [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ are ionisation isomers. (ii) What is meant by the 'Chelate effect'? Give an example.

key_points: (i) Add BaCl₂ solution: [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl gives white precipitate of BaSO₄ (SO₄²⁻ is outside the coordination sphere, free in solution), while [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ also gives white precipitate. Alternatively, add AgNO₃: [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl gives white precipitate of AgCl (Cl⁻ is free), while [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ gives no precipitate with AgNO₃.

(ii) Chelate effect: The enhanced stability of a complex containing chelate rings (formed by polydentate ligands) compared to a similar complex containing monodentate ligands. Example: [Cu(en)₂]²⁺ is more stable than [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.

sub_questions.solution: For part (i): When aqueous AgNO₃ solution is added, [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl gives a white precipitate of AgCl because Cl⁻ is present as a free ion outside the coordination sphere. [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ gives no precipitate with AgNO₃ but gives a white precipitate with BaCl₂ solution (BaSO₄) because SO₄²⁻ is free outside. This confirms they are ionisation isomers — they have the same molecular formula but different ions inside and outside the coordination sphere. For part (ii): The chelate effect refers to the extra stability of complexes formed by polydentate (chelating) ligands compared to complexes formed by the equivalent number of monodentate ligands. This increased stability arises due to a more favourable entropy change when polydentate ligands replace monodentate ligands. Example: [Cu(en)₂]²⁺ (with bidentate ethylenediamine) is more stable than [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ (with monodentate ammonia).

questions.solution: See sub_questions for detailed answers to both options (a) and (b).

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के मध्य अंतर कीजिए : (i) पेप्टाइड बंध और ग्लाइकोसाइडी बंध  (ii) आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल और अनावश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल
questions.text_english: Differentiate between the following : (i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage  (ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids

sub_questions.text: (i) पेप्टाइड बंध और ग्लाइकोसाइडी बंध
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage

key_points: Peptide linkage: amide bond (–CO–NH–) formed between amino group of one amino acid and carboxyl group of another amino acid during protein synthesis.
Glycosidic linkage: an ether-type bond (–C–O–C–) formed between two monosaccharide units via an –OH group, as in disaccharides and polysaccharides.

sub_questions.solution: A peptide linkage is an amide bond (–CO–NH–) formed when the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid reacts with the amino group (–NH₂) of another amino acid with the loss of a water molecule. It is found in proteins and polypeptides. A glycosidic linkage, on the other hand, is an ether-type bond (–C–O–C–) formed between the anomeric carbon of one monosaccharide and a hydroxyl group of another monosaccharide with the elimination of water. It is found in disaccharides (e.g., maltose, sucrose) and polysaccharides (e.g., starch, cellulose).

sub_questions.text: (ii) आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल और अनावश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल
sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids

key_points: Essential amino acids: cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet. Examples: valine, leucine, lysine.
Non-essential amino acids: can be synthesized by the human body from other metabolites and do not need to be consumed in the diet. Examples: glycine, alanine, aspartic acid.

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesized by the human body in adequate amounts and must therefore be supplied through food. There are approximately 10 essential amino acids, including valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, threonine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, methionine, histidine, and arginine. Non-essential amino acids are those that the body can synthesize on its own from other available metabolic intermediates, so they do not necessarily need to come from the diet. Examples include glycine, alanine, serine, aspartic acid, and glutamic acid.

questions.solution: See sub_questions for answers to both parts.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया एक चरण में सम्पन्न होती है : 2A + B → 2C. उपरोक्त अभिक्रिया का वेग किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होगा, यदि अभिक्रिया पात्र का आयतन उसके मूल आयतन से घटाकर एक तिहाई कर दिया जाए ? इस घटे हुए आयतन के साथ अभिक्रिया कोटि में क्या कोई परिवर्तन होगा ?
questions.text_english: Following reaction takes place in one step : 2A + B → 2C. How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?

key_points: Rate = k[A]²[B]. Decreasing volume to 1/3 triples all concentrations: [A] becomes 3[A] and [B] becomes 3[B].
New rate = k(3[A])²(3[B]) = k × 9[A]² × 3[B] = 27 × k[A]²[B]. Rate increases 27 times.
Order of reaction does not change; it remains 3rd order (2+1). Order is an intrinsic property of the reaction mechanism.

questions.solution: Since the reaction 2A + B → 2C takes place in one step, it is an elementary reaction and the rate law is Rate = k[A]²[B], making it a third-order reaction overall. When the volume is decreased to one-third of its original value, all concentrations are tripled: [A] becomes 3[A] and [B] becomes 3[B]. The new rate = k(3[A])²(3[B]) = k × 9[A]² × 3[B] = 27k[A]²[B]. Therefore, the rate of reaction increases by 27 times. The order of the reaction, however, does not change. Order is determined by the reaction mechanism and is an intrinsic property of the reaction — it remains third order regardless of the volume of the vessel.

questions.text: किसी प्रथम कोटि के तापीय विघटन अभिक्रिया के लिए निम्न आँकड़े प्राप्त हुए : C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g). क्रम संख्या 1: समय = 0 s, कुल दाब = 0.30 atm; क्रम संख्या 2: समय = 30 s, कुल दाब = 0.50 atm. वेग स्थिरांक की गणना कीजिए। [दिया है : log 3 = 0.48]
questions.text_english: For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained : C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g). S.No. 1: Time = 0 s, Total Pressure = 0.30 atm; S.No. 2: Time = 30 s, Total Pressure = 0.50 atm. Calculate rate constant. [Given : log 3 = 0.48]

key_points: At t=0: P₀ = 0.30 atm (only C₂H₅Cl). At t=30s: C₂H₅Cl = P₀ − x, C₂H₄ = x, HCl = x; total = P₀ + x = 0.50, so x = 0.20 atm.

questions.image_description: A data table with two rows: S.No. 1 — Time(s) = 0, Total Pressure (atm) = 0.30; S.No. 2 — Time(s) = 30, Total Pressure (atm) = 0.50.
questions.solution: For the reaction C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g), let the initial pressure of C₂H₅Cl be P₀ = 0.30 atm and let x be the decrease in pressure after time t. At time t = 30 s, the total pressure = (P₀ − x) + x + x = P₀ + x = 0.50 atm. Therefore, x = 0.50 − 0.30 = 0.20 atm. The partial pressure of C₂H₅Cl at t = 30 s is P = P₀ − x = 0.30 − 0.20 = 0.10 atm. Applying the first order rate equation: k = (2.303/t) × log(P₀/P) = (2.303/30) × log(0.30/0.10) = (2.303/30) × log 3 = (2.303/30) × 0.48 = 1.106/30 ≈ 0.0369 s⁻¹. Therefore, the rate constant k ≈ 3.69 × 10⁻² s⁻¹.

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: (a) निम्नलिखित के उत्तर दीजिए: (i) साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc), E°(सेल) से तो संबंधित है, लेकिन E(सेल) से नहीं। क्यों ? (ii) दो धातुओं 'A' और 'B' के मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव क्रमशः –0.24 V और +0.80 V हैं। इनमें से कौन तनु H₂SO₄ से हाइड्रोजन गैस निर्मुक्त करेगी ? (iii) लेड संचायक बैटरी को आवेशित करते समय होने वाली सेल अभिक्रिया लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Answer the following: (i) Why is Kc related to E°cell and not to Ecell ? (ii) Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of –0.24 V and +0.80 V respectively. Which will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. H₂SO₄ ? (iii) Write the cell reaction which occurs in lead storage battery when it is in charging.

key_points: (i) Kc is related to E°cell because both E°cell and Kc refer to standard conditions (unit activities/concentrations). The equation ΔG° = −nFE°cell = −RT ln Kc connects standard values. Ecell (non-standard) depends on concentrations via Nernst equation and keeps changing, so it cannot be used directly to calculate Kc.

(ii) Metal 'A' (E° = –0.24 V) will liberate H₂ from dil. H₂SO₄, because its electrode potential is negative meaning it is more easily oxidised than H₂. Metal 'B' (E° = +0.80 V) is nobler than hydrogen and cannot displace it.
(iii) Charging of lead storage battery — at cathode: PbSO₄ + 2e⁻ → Pb + SO₄²⁻; at anode: PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → PbO₂ + SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻; overall: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄.

sub_questions.solution: For (i): Kc is related to E°cell (standard cell EMF) and not to Ecell because the relationship ΔG° = −nFE°cell = −RT ln Kc holds only under standard conditions. The standard cell EMF E°cell is measured when all species are at unit activity (standard state), which is the same condition under which Kc is defined. The actual cell EMF Ecell depends on the current concentrations through the Nernst equation and continuously changes during the cell reaction, making it unsuitable for establishing a constant equilibrium relationship. For (ii): Metal A with E° = –0.24 V is more active than hydrogen (E° = 0 V), meaning it can be oxidised by H⁺ ions in dilute H₂SO₄ to liberate H₂ gas. Metal B with E° = +0.80 V is less active (nobler) than hydrogen and will not displace hydrogen from acid. For (iii): During charging of a lead storage battery, the reactions are reversed. At cathode: PbSO₄ + 2e⁻ → Pb + SO₄²⁻; at anode: PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → PbO₂ + SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻; overall: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄.

sub_questions.text: (b) मर्क्यूरी सेल किस प्रकार की बैटरी है ? शुष्क सेल की तुलना में यह क्यों अधिक फ़ायदेमंद है ? मर्क्यूरी सेल में होने वाली समग्र अभिक्रिया लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What type of battery is Mercury cell ? Why it is more advantageous than dry cell ? Write overall reaction taking place in Mercury cell.

key_points: Mercury cell is a primary battery (non-rechargeable).
Advantage over dry cell: Mercury cell provides a constant cell voltage throughout its life (~1.35 V) unlike a dry cell whose voltage decreases gradually during use.
Overall reaction: Zn(s) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l)

sub_questions.solution: A mercury cell is a primary cell (non-rechargeable battery). It is more advantageous than a dry cell because it provides a constant, steady voltage of approximately 1.35 V throughout its entire working life, whereas the voltage of a dry cell decreases gradually as it is used due to the changing concentrations of electrolyte and reactants. This makes mercury cells especially useful in hearing aids, watches, and calculators where a stable voltage is essential. The anode consists of zinc amalgam and the cathode is a paste of HgO mixed with KOH. The overall reaction taking place in a mercury cell is: Zn(s) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l).

questions.solution: See sub_questions for complete answers to options (a) and (b).

questions.text: 0.61 g बेन्जोइक अम्ल (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 122 g mol⁻¹) को 5 g CS₂ में घोलने पर, जिसमें यह 88% तक द्वितय बनाता है, बने विलयन का क्वथनांक ज्ञात कीजिए। CS₂ का क्वथनांक और Kb क्रमशः 46.2 °C और 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ है।
questions.text_english: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing 0.61 g of benzoic acid (Molar mass = 122 g mol⁻¹) in 5 g of CS₂ in which it dimerises to the extent of 88%. The boiling point and Kb of CS₂ are 46.2 °C and 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.

key_points: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol.
For dimerisation: 2C₆H₅COOH ⇌ (C₆H₅COOH)₂. If α = 0.88, van't Hoff factor i = 1 − α/2 = 1 − 0.44 = 0.56.
Boiling point = 46.2 + 1.288 ≈ 47.49 °C.

questions.solution: Moles of benzoic acid = 0.61/122 = 0.005 mol. For dimerisation of benzoic acid in CS₂: 2C₆H₅COOH ⇌ (C₆H₅COOH)₂. If degree of dimerisation α = 0.88, the van't Hoff factor is i = (1 − α/2) = 1 − 0.88/2 = 1 − 0.44 = 0.56. Molality m = (0.005 mol)/(5 × 10⁻³ kg) = 0.005/0.005 = 1 mol kg⁻¹. Elevation in boiling point ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 0.56 × 2.3 × 1 = 1.288 K. Boiling point of solution = 46.2 + 1.288 = 47.488 ≈ 47.49 °C.
questions.topic: Elevation in Boiling Point, Van't Hoff Factor, Association

questions.text: D-ग्लूकोस की निम्नलिखित के साथ अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए : (a) HI  (b) Br₂ जल  (c) सांद्र HNO₃
questions.text_english: Write the reactions of D-Glucose with the following : (a) HI  (b) Br₂ water  (c) Conc. HNO₃

sub_questions.text: (a) HI
sub_questions.text_english: (a) HI

key_points: D-Glucose + HI (red P) → n-hexane (hexan-1-ol intermediate then reduction). The –OH groups and –CHO are reduced. Product: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (n-hexane).

sub_questions.solution: D-Glucose reacts with HI (hydroiodic acid, red phosphorus) to give n-hexane. This reaction involves the reduction of all the –OH groups and the aldehyde group to –H groups, confirming the straight-chain hexane structure of glucose. The reaction is: C₆H₁₂O₆ + HI/Red P → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (n-hexane) + H₂O + HI (consumed). This proves that glucose has a 6-carbon straight chain.

sub_questions.text: (b) Br₂ जल
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Br₂ water

key_points: D-Glucose + Br₂/H₂O → D-Gluconic acid (oxidation of –CHO to –COOH only).

sub_questions.solution: D-Glucose reacts with bromine water (Br₂/H₂O) to undergo mild oxidation. The aldehyde group (–CHO) of glucose is selectively oxidised to a carboxyl group (–COOH), giving D-gluconic acid (glucono-δ-lactone intermediate). The reaction is: CH₂OH(CHOH)₄CHO + Br₂ + H₂O → CH₂OH(CHOH)₄COOH + 2HBr. This reaction also decolourises bromine water, confirming the presence of an aldehyde group in glucose.

sub_questions.text: (c) सांद्र HNO₃
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Conc. HNO₃

key_points: D-Glucose + conc. HNO₃ → D-Saccharic acid (glucaric acid). Both –CHO and –CH₂OH are oxidised to –COOH.

sub_questions.solution: When D-glucose reacts with concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃), a stronger oxidising agent is involved, and both the aldehyde group (–CHO) and the primary alcohol group (–CH₂OH) are oxidised to carboxyl groups (–COOH). The product is D-saccharic acid (also called glucaric acid): HOOC(CHOH)₄COOH. This confirms that glucose has a terminal aldehyde group at one end and a primary alcohol group at the other end of the chain.

questions.solution: See sub_questions for detailed reactions of D-glucose with HI, Br₂ water, and conc. HNO₃.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (a) कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक समतुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों से उच्च होते हैं। (b) ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है। (c) अमोनिया और इसके व्युत्पन्नों का कार्बोनिल समूह के साथ नाभिकरागी संयोजन प्रबल अम्लीय माध्यम में नहीं होता है।
questions.text_english: Give reasons for the following : (a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses. (b) Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature. (c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

sub_questions.text: (a) कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्लों के क्वथनांक समतुल्य आण्विक द्रव्यमान वाले ऐल्कोहॉलों से उच्च होते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.

key_points: Carboxylic acids form stable cyclic dimers through two intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H···O=C), effectively doubling their molecular mass in solution/vapour phase, requiring much more energy to vaporise. Alcohols form only one H-bond per molecule.

sub_questions.solution: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular masses because carboxylic acid molecules form very stable cyclic dimers through two intermolecular hydrogen bonds — each –COOH group forms a hydrogen bond with the –COOH group of another molecule (O–H···O=C). This dimerisation effectively doubles the molecular mass in the liquid/vapour phase, requiring much more energy to break these associations and vaporise. Alcohols can form only one hydrogen bond per molecule through –OH groups, which is weaker and less extensive than the dimerisation in carboxylic acids.

sub_questions.text: (b) ऐल्डिहाइडों और कीटोनों के α-हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Alpha (α) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.

key_points: The α-carbon is adjacent to the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group (–C=O). The carbonyl group withdraws electron density inductively and by resonance, making the C–H bond at the α-carbon weaker and the α-hydrogen more easily removed as H⁺ (acidic). The carbanion formed is stabilised by resonance (enolate ion).

sub_questions.solution: The α-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic because they are attached to a carbon (α-carbon) adjacent to the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group (C=O). The carbonyl group withdraws electron density from the α-carbon through inductive effect and also stabilises the negative charge on the α-carbanion (formed after loss of H⁺) through resonance, forming a resonance-stabilised enolate ion. The delocalisation of the negative charge across the oxygen atom of the enolate stabilises the conjugate base, making the removal of α-hydrogen relatively easy, thus conferring acidic character to α-hydrogens.

sub_questions.text: (c) अमोनिया और इसके व्युत्पन्नों का कार्बोनिल समूह के साथ नाभिकरागी संयोजन प्रबल अम्लीय माध्यम में नहीं होता है।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.

key_points: In strongly acidic medium, ammonia and its derivatives (–NH₂ compounds) get protonated to form –NH₃⁺, making them positively charged. A protonated (cationic) species cannot act as a nucleophile because it lacks a lone pair of electrons available for attack. Hence, nucleophilic addition does not occur.

sub_questions.solution: In strongly acidic medium, ammonia (NH₃) and its derivatives (like hydroxylamine, hydrazine, semicarbazide, etc.) get protonated. For example, NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. The protonated species (–NH₃⁺) carries a positive charge and has no available lone pair of electrons to act as a nucleophile. Since nucleophilic addition requires the nucleophile to donate its lone pair of electrons to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, the protonated amine cannot initiate the attack. Therefore, nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives to carbonyl compounds does not occur in strongly acidic medium.

questions.solution: See sub_questions for detailed reasons for each part.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित से संबद्ध अभिक्रिया लिखिए : (a) राइमर–टीमन अभिक्रिया  (b) कोल्बे अभिक्रिया  (c) ऐनिसोल की फ्रीडेल–क्राफ्ट ऐसिलन अभिक्रिया
questions.text_english: Write the reaction involved in the following : (a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction  (b) Kolbe's reaction  (c) Friedal-Crafts acylation of anisole

sub_questions.text: (a) राइमर–टीमन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction

key_points: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH (aq) → Salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as major product. The reaction introduces a –CHO group ortho to the –OH group of phenol.

sub_questions.solution: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl₃) and sodium hydroxide solution. The intermediate dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) generated from CHCl₃ and NaOH acts as the electrophile and attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion. On hydrolysis, the resulting intermediate gives salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) as the major product. Reaction: C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + 3NaOH → 2-HOC₆H₄CHO (salicylaldehyde) + 3NaCl + 2H₂O.

sub_questions.text: (b) कोल्बे अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Kolbe's reaction

key_points: Sodium phenoxide + CO₂ (at 400 K, 4–7 atm pressure) → sodium salicylate; on acidification gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid).

sub_questions.solution: In Kolbe's reaction (also called Kolbe-Schmitt reaction), sodium phenoxide (C₆H₅ONa) is treated with carbon dioxide gas under high pressure (4–7 atm) at about 400 K. CO₂ acts as a weak electrophile and attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ring. The product, sodium salicylate, on acidification gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Reaction: C₆H₅ONa + CO₂ → (400 K, 4–7 atm) → C₆H₄(OH)(COONa); on acidification → C₆H₄(OH)(COOH) (salicylic acid).

sub_questions.text: (c) ऐनिसोल की फ्रीडेल–क्राफ्ट ऐसिलन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Friedal-Crafts acylation of anisole

key_points: Anisole + CH₃COCl (acyl chloride) + anhydrous AlCl₃ (Lewis acid catalyst) → para-methoxyacetophenone (major, as –OCH₃ is ortho/para director) + ortho product (minor).

sub_questions.solution: In the Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole, anisole (methoxybenzene, C₆H₅OCH₃) reacts with acetyl chloride (CH₃COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ as a Lewis acid catalyst. The acylium ion (CH₃CO⁺) generated acts as the electrophile. Since the –OCH₃ group is an ortho/para director and activates the ring, the acyl group enters preferentially at the para position. The major product is p-methoxyacetophenone (4-methoxyphenyl methyl ketone, para product). Reaction: C₆H₅OCH₃ + CH₃COCl → (AlCl₃) → p-CH₃O·C₆H₄·COCH₃ + HCl.

questions.text: C₄H₉Br आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X', जलीय KOH के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक ऐल्कोहॉल देता है। इस अभिक्रिया का वेग केवल यौगिक 'X' की सांद्रता पर निर्भर करता है। जब यौगिक 'X' के ध्रुवण घूर्णक समावयव 'Y' को जलीय KOH विलयन के साथ अभिक्रियित किया गया तो अभिक्रिया वेग यौगिक 'Y' की सांद्रता और जलीय KOH दोनों पर निर्भर पाया गया। (a) 'X' और 'Y' दोनों के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए। (b) 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन रेसिमीकरण करेगा और क्यों ? (c) 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन विन्यास के प्रतिलोमन के साथ उत्पाद बनाएगा और क्यों ?
questions.text_english: Compound 'X' with molecular formula C₄H₉Br reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous KOH solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous KOH both. (a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'. (b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ? (c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?

sub_questions.text: (a) 'X' और 'Y' दोनों के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.

key_points: X: (CH₃)₃CBr — 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tertiary butyl bromide), rate depends only on [X] → SN1 mechanism.
Y: CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃ — 2-bromobutane (optically active, secondary), rate depends on [Y] and [KOH] → SN2 mechanism.

sub_questions.solution: Compound X reacts by SN1 mechanism (rate depends only on [X]) and has molecular formula C₄H₉Br, so it must be a tertiary halide: X is (CH₃)₃CBr (2-bromo-2-methylpropane / tert-butyl bromide). Compound Y is an optically active isomer of X reacting by SN2 mechanism (rate depends on both [Y] and [KOH]), so Y must be a secondary halide with a chiral centre: Y is CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃ (2-bromobutane).

sub_questions.text: (b) 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन रेसिमीकरण करेगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?

key_points: X undergoes racemisation because it reacts via SN1 mechanism, forming a planar carbocation intermediate. The nucleophile (OH⁻) can attack from either face of the planar carbocation, giving equal amounts of R and S products (racemic mixture).

sub_questions.solution: Compound X [(CH₃)₃CBr] will undergo racemisation. X reacts via the SN1 mechanism. In the first step, (CH₃)₃CBr ionises to form a stable tertiary carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺, which is planar (sp² hybridised). The nucleophile OH⁻ can attack this planar carbocation from either the front or the back face with equal probability, giving a racemic mixture of R and S products in equal amounts. The result is racemisation — equal amounts of both enantiomers, so the net optical rotation becomes zero.

sub_questions.text: (c) 'X' और 'Y' में से कौन विन्यास के प्रतिलोमन के साथ उत्पाद बनाएगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?

key_points: Y undergoes inversion of configuration (Walden inversion) because it reacts via SN2 mechanism. The nucleophile (OH⁻) attacks from the back side of the C–Br bond in a single concerted step, resulting in 100% inversion of configuration at the chiral centre (Walden inversion).

sub_questions.solution: Compound Y [CH₃CH₂CH(Br)CH₃] will form the product with inversion of configuration (Walden inversion). Y reacts by the SN2 mechanism, which proceeds in a single concerted step. The nucleophile OH⁻ attacks the chiral carbon from the side exactly opposite to the leaving group Br⁻ (backside attack). This backside attack inverts the spatial arrangement of the three remaining groups at the chiral centre — similar to an umbrella turning inside out. Since the reaction is concerted and the attack is always from the back, 100% inversion of configuration occurs at the chiral centre, giving the product with opposite configuration.

questions.text: ऐमीनों की खनिज अम्लों से अभिक्रिया द्वारा अमोनियम लवणों का बनना इनकी क्षारकीय प्रकृति को दर्शाता है। ऐलीफैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया की अपेक्षा प्रबल क्षारक होते हैं जबकि ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया से दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं। ऐलीफैटिक तथा ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक एवं द्वितीयक ऐमीन ऐसिड क्लोराइड, ऐनहाइड्राइड और ऐस्टर से नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया करते हैं। ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन की इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं में मुख्य समस्या इनकी उच्च अभिक्रियाशीलता है। प्रतिस्थापन ऑर्थों तथा पैरा दोनों स्थानों पर हो सकता है। हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक प्राथमिक, द्वितीयक एवं तृतीयक ऐमीनों की पहचान एवं विभेद के लिए प्रयोग में लाया जाता है। प्रायः ऐरिलऐमीन से प्राप्त किये जाने वाले ऐरिलडाइऐज़ोनियम लवण, विभिन्न प्रकार के नाभिकरागियों द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किए जाते हैं जिसके द्वारा ऐरिल हैलाइड, सायनाइड, फ़ीनॉल तथा ऐरीन प्राप्त करने की लाभप्रद विधि उपलब्ध होती है।
questions.text_english: The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that these are basic in nature. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia whereas aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia. Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their high reactivity. Substitution tends to occur at ortho- and para-positions. Hinsberg reagent is used for the identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, usually obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group with a variety of nucleophiles to provide advantageous methods for producing aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

sub_questions.text: (a)(i) जलीय विलयन में (CH₃)₃N की तुलना में CH₃–NH₂ प्रबल क्षारक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a)(i) Why CH₃–NH₂ is a stronger base than (CH₃)₃N in aqueous solution ?

key_points: In aqueous solution, solvation of the protonated cation (ammonium ion) plays a key role. CH₃NH₃⁺ has three N–H bonds and can form more hydrogen bonds with water than (CH₃)₃NH⁺ which has only one N–H bond. Greater solvation of CH₃NH₃⁺ stabilises it more, making CH₃NH₂ a stronger base in aqueous solution despite trimethylamine having more electron-donating methyl groups.

sub_questions.solution: In the gas phase, (CH₃)₃N would be a stronger base due to more electron-donating methyl groups. However, in aqueous solution, the basicity is also determined by the solvation of the protonated form. CH₃NH₂ on protonation gives CH₃NH₃⁺, which has three N–H bonds and can form three hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making it well-solvated and stable. In contrast, (CH₃)₃NH⁺ has only one N–H bond and can form only one hydrogen bond with water, so it is less solvated. Since CH₃NH₃⁺ is more stabilised by solvation in aqueous solution, the equilibrium shifts more towards protonation, making CH₃NH₂ a stronger base than (CH₃)₃N in aqueous solution.

sub_questions.text: (a)(ii) यौगिक A और B के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखिए : CH₃CONH₂ → (NaOBr) → A → (C₆H₅COCl / क्षार) → B
sub_questions.text_english: (a)(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B : CH₃CONH₂ → (NaOBr) → A → (C₆H₅COCl / Base) → B

key_points: A: CH₃NH₂ (methylamine) — Hoffmann bromamide degradation of acetamide gives methylamine (one carbon less).
B: C₆H₅CO–NH–CH₃ (N-methylbenzamide) — reaction of methylamine with benzoyl chloride in the presence of base gives N-methylbenzamide.

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: CH₃CONH₂ (acetamide) reacts with NaOBr (Hoffmann bromamide reaction / Hoffmann degradation). In this reaction, the amide loses one carbon to give a primary amine with one fewer carbon: A = CH₃NH₂ (methylamine). Step 2: CH₃NH₂ (methylamine) reacts with C₆H₅COCl (benzoyl chloride) in the presence of a base (Schotten-Baumann reaction). The amine acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzoyl chloride, and the base neutralises the HCl produced: B = C₆H₅CONHCH₃ (N-methylbenzamide).

sub_questions.text: (b) C₃H₉N आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'X' हिन्सबर्ग अभिकर्मक के साथ अभिक्रिया करके एक उत्पाद देता है जो क्षार में अविलेय है। 'X' की पहचान कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) A compound 'X' with molecular formula C₃H₉N reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.

key_points: X is a secondary amine — N,N-dimethylmethylamine is not possible (that would be trimethylamine, tertiary). C₃H₉N secondary amine: CH₃–NH–C₂H₅ (N-methylethylamine). Hinsberg reagent gives a sulphonamide with secondary amines that has no N–H bond, so it is insoluble in alkali.

sub_questions.solution: Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride, C₆H₅SO₂Cl) reacts differently with primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. With secondary amines, it forms a sulphonamide that has no N–H bond (since both H atoms on N are replaced by the sulphonyl group and the alkyl group). Without an N–H bond, the sulphonamide cannot ionise in alkali and is therefore insoluble in alkali. The compound X with formula C₃H₉N that is a secondary amine is N-methylethylamine (CH₃–NH–C₂H₅). Therefore, X = CH₃–NH–C₂H₅ (or diethylamine is C₄H₁₁N, so for C₃H₉N: N-methylethylamine). Primary amines give N-H containing sulphonamides soluble in alkali; tertiary amines do not react at all.

sub_questions.text: (b) (वैकल्पिक) आप ऐनिलीन को बेन्जोनाइट्राइल में कैसे रूपांतरित कर सकते हो ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) (Alternative) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?

key_points: Aniline → (NaNO₂ + HCl, 0–5°C) → Benzenediazonium chloride → (CuCN / Sandmeyer reaction) → Benzonitrile.

sub_questions.solution: Aniline can be converted to benzonitrile in two steps via the Sandmeyer reaction. First, aniline is diazotised by treating with NaNO₂ and HCl at 0–5°C to give benzenediazonium chloride (C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻). Then, the diazonium salt is treated with CuCN (cuprous cyanide) — the Sandmeyer reaction — where the diazonium group (–N₂⁺) is replaced by the cyanide group (–CN), giving benzonitrile (C₆H₅CN). Reaction: C₆H₅NH₂ → (NaNO₂/HCl, 0°C) → C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ → (CuCN) → C₆H₅CN.

sub_questions.text: (c) नाइट्रोकरण करने से पहले ऐनिलीन के –NH₂ समूह का ऐसीटिलन क्यों किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Why is –NH₂ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?

key_points: 1. To protect the –NH₂ group from oxidation by the acidic nitrating mixture (HNO₃ + H₂SO₄).

2. Acetylation reduces the strong activating effect of –NH₂ to a milder level, reducing the reactivity and preventing polynitration (di- or tri-nitration), giving predominantly the para-nitro product.

sub_questions.solution: The –NH₂ group of aniline is acetylated before nitration for two important reasons. First, the free –NH₂ group is susceptible to oxidation by the strong acidic nitrating mixture (HNO₃ + H₂SO₄), which would destroy the amine group or give undesired side products. Acetylation converts –NH₂ to –NHCOCH₃ (acetamido group), which is stable under nitrating conditions. Second, the –NH₂ group is a very powerful activator of the benzene ring and would cause polynitration (di- or trisubstitution). Acetylation moderates the electron-donating power of nitrogen, allowing controlled mononitration predominantly at the para position. After nitration, the acetyl group can be hydrolysed to regenerate –NH₂.

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनाने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार तथा ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण करता है। क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत (CFT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केंद्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव (लिगन्डों को बिंदु आवेश मानते हुए उनके द्वारा प्रदत्त प्रभाव) पर आधारित है। प्रबल क्षेत्र तथा दुर्बल क्षेत्र में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. The Crystal Field Theory (CFT) of coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by the ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

sub_questions.text: (a) अष्टफलकीय क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र में किन d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा में वृद्धि होती है जब लिगन्ड केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के समीप जाता है ? अपने उत्तर के समर्थन में कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.

key_points: In an octahedral crystal field, the eg set (dx²-y² and dz²) have their energies raised. These orbitals point directly along the x, y, z axes where the six ligands approach. Direct electrostatic repulsion between ligand electron pairs and the electrons in these axially-directed d-orbitals raises their energy. The t2g set (dxy, dyz, dxz) point between axes and are less repelled, so their energy is lowered.

sub_questions.solution: In an octahedral crystal field, the energies of the eg set of d-orbitals — namely dx²-y² and dz² — are raised when ligands approach the central metal atom. In an octahedral complex, six ligands approach the central metal ion along the ±x, ±y, and ±z axes. The dx²-y² orbital has its lobes directed along the x and y axes, and the dz² orbital has its main lobe along the z-axis. Since these orbitals point directly towards the incoming ligands, there is maximum electrostatic repulsion between the electron pairs of the ligands and the electrons in these orbitals, raising their energy above the barycentre. The other three d-orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz), collectively called the t2g set, have their lobes directed between the axes, so they experience less repulsion and their energy is relatively lowered.

sub_questions.text: (b) क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत का उपयोग करके, निम्नलिखित के केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए : (i) [CoF₆]³⁻  (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺  [परमाणु क्रमांक : Co = 27]
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following : (i) [CoF₆]³⁻  (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺  [At. No. : Co = 27]

key_points: Co³⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁶. (i) [CoF₆]³⁻: F⁻ is a weak field ligand → high spin → t2g⁴eg² (4 electrons in t2g, 2 in eg). (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: NH₃ is a strong field ligand → low spin → t2g⁶eg⁰ (all 6 electrons in t2g).

sub_questions.solution: Co has atomic number 27, configuration [Ar]3d⁷4s². Co³⁺ loses 3 electrons (4s² and one 3d electron) to give configuration [Ar]3d⁶ (6 d-electrons). For (i) [CoF₆]³⁻: F⁻ is a weak-field ligand, producing a small crystal field splitting energy (Δo). With 6 d-electrons and small Δo, the pairing energy is greater than Δo, so electrons occupy both t2g and eg orbitals following Hund's rule (high spin configuration): t2g⁴ eg² — with 4 unpaired electrons. For (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: NH₃ is a strong-field ligand producing large Δo. With large Δo, all 6 d-electrons are forced to pair in the lower t2g level (low spin): t2g⁶ eg⁰ — diamagnetic with zero unpaired electrons.

sub_questions.text: (c) [NiCl₄]²⁻ अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Ni(CO)₄] प्रतिचुंबकीय है यद्यपि दोनों चतुष्फलकीय हैं। क्यों ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english: (c) [NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)₄] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]

key_points: Ni in [NiCl₄]²⁻ is Ni²⁺ (3d⁸): Cl⁻ is a weak-field ligand, no pairing → 2 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic. Ni in [Ni(CO)₄] is Ni⁰ (3d¹⁰): CO is a strong-field ligand and Ni⁰ has a fully filled 3d¹⁰ configuration → no unpaired electrons → diamagnetic.

sub_questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28 with configuration [Ar]3d⁸4s². In [NiCl₄]²⁻, nickel is in the +2 oxidation state (Ni²⁺) with configuration 3d⁸. Cl⁻ is a weak-field ligand and does not cause pairing of d-electrons. The 3d⁸ configuration of Ni²⁺ in the presence of Cl⁻ leaves 2 unpaired electrons, making [NiCl₄]²⁻ paramagnetic. In [Ni(CO)₄], nickel is in the zero oxidation state (Ni⁰) with configuration 3d⁸4s² in the free atom, but CO is a very strong-field ligand that causes promotion of 4s electrons and complete pairing of all d-electrons. The effective configuration becomes 3d¹⁰ for Ni⁰ in the complex (or all electrons are paired in d and the hybridisation is sp³). With no unpaired electrons, [Ni(CO)₄] is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: (c) (वैकल्पिक) संकुल [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ का संकरण एवं चुंबकीय व्यवहार लिखिए। [परमाणु क्रमांक : Fe = 26]
sub_questions.text_english: (c) (Alternative) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]

key_points: Fe³⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁵ (5 d-electrons). CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand → electrons pair in 3d → d²sp³ hybridisation → octahedral geometry → 1 unpaired electron → paramagnetic.

sub_questions.solution: Fe has atomic number 26, configuration [Ar]3d⁶4s². Fe³⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁵ (5 d-electrons). CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand that causes pairing of electrons. In the presence of CN⁻, the 5 d-electrons pair up in two 3d orbitals (t2g set), leaving one 3d orbital, one 4s orbital, and three 4p orbitals empty. These 6 orbitals hybridise to give d²sp³ hybridisation, forming an octahedral geometry. After pairing: configuration is t2g⁵ eg⁰ with one unpaired electron. Therefore, [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has d²sp³ hybridisation, octahedral geometry, and is paramagnetic (1 unpaired electron).

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: (a)(i) किसी कार्बनिक यौगिक (X) का आण्विक सूत्र C₅H₁₀O है। (X) की संरचनाएँ बनाइए यदि यह : (I) टॉलेन परीक्षण नहीं देता परन्तु धनात्मक आयडोफॉर्म परीक्षण देता है। (II) टॉलेन परीक्षण और आयडोफॉर्म परीक्षण नहीं देता, लेकिन ऐल्डॉल संघनन करता है। (III) कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया करता है। (a)(ii) दर्शाइए कि निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक यौगिक को कैसे बेन्जोइक अम्ल में रूपांतरित किया जा सकता है ? (I) ऐसीटोफ़ीनोन  (II) एथिलबेन्जीन
sub_questions.text_english:
(a)(i) An organic compound (X) has the molecular formula C₅H₁₀O. Draw structures for (X) if it : (I) does not give Tollen's test but gives a positive iodoform test. (II) does not give Tollen's test and iodoform test but undergoes Aldol condensation. (III) undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction.
(a)(ii) Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid : (I) Acetophenone  (II) Ethyl benzene

key_points: (i)(I) Does not give Tollens' (not aldehyde), gives iodoform (CH₃CO– group present) → methyl ketone. C₅H₁₀O methyl ketone: CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ (pentan-2-one) or CH₃COC₂H₅ is C₄H₈O — so pentan-2-one: CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃.

(i)(II) No Tollens', no iodoform, undergoes Aldol → aldehyde without alpha H or ketone without CH₃CO group. C₅H₁₀O: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CHO (pentanal) — has alpha H but no CH₃CO group, gives Tollens'. So this is a ketone with alpha H but not methyl ketone: (CH₃CH₂)₂CO diethyl ketone (pentan-3-one) — does not give Tollens' ✓, does not give iodoform ✓, has alpha-H → Aldol condensation ✓.
(i)(III) Cannizzaro reaction occurs with aldehydes having no alpha-H. C₅H₁₀O with no alpha-H aldehyde: (CH₃)₃CCHO (2,2-dimethylpropanal / pivaldehyde).
(ii)(I) Acetophenone → (NaOI or Cl₂/NaOH, iodoform reaction) → Benzoate salt → acid → Benzoic acid. Or: C₆H₅COCH₃ + Cl₂/NaOH → C₆H₅COONa + CHCl₃ → C₆H₅COOH (benzoic acid).
(ii)(II) Ethylbenzene → (KMnO₄/H⁺, oxidation) → Benzoic acid. C₆H₅CH₂CH₃ → (KMnO₄, acidified) → C₆H₅COOH.

sub_questions.solution: For (i)(I): The compound does not give Tollens' test so it is not an aldehyde, but gives a positive iodoform test, indicating the presence of a –COCH₃ (methyl ketone) group. With molecular formula C₅H₁₀O, the structure is pentan-2-one: CH₃–CO–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃. For (i)(II): No Tollens' test (not aldehyde), no iodoform test (no –COCH₃), but undergoes Aldol condensation (has α-H adjacent to carbonyl). This must be a ketone without a methyl group on carbonyl. The structure is pentan-3-one (diethyl ketone): CH₃CH₂–CO–CH₂CH₃. It has α-H for Aldol, is a ketone (no Tollens'), and has no –COCH₃ group (no iodoform). For (i)(III): Cannizzaro reaction requires an aldehyde with no α-hydrogen (no α-H). With formula C₅H₁₀O, the structure is 2,2-dimethylpropanal (pivaldehyde): (CH₃)₃C–CHO. The quaternary α-carbon has no H atoms. For (ii)(I): Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) can be converted to benzoic acid by the haloform reaction using Cl₂/NaOH or I₂/NaOH (iodoform reaction). The –COCH₃ group is oxidised to –COO⁻ (as sodium benzoate), which on acidification gives benzoic acid (C₆H₅COOH). For (ii)(II): Ethylbenzene (C₆H₅CH₂CH₃) is oxidised by acidified KMnO₄ solution. The alkyl side chain is oxidised to –COOH regardless of its length. The product is benzoic acid (C₆H₅COOH).

sub_questions.text: (b) निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए : (i) बेन्जैल्डिहाइड के 2,4-डाइनाइट्रोफ़ेनिल हाइड्रेज़ोन व्युत्पन्न की संरचना बनाइए। (ii) निम्नलिखित को उनकी HCN के प्रति अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए : डाइ–तृतीयक ब्यूटिल कीटोन, ऐसीटैल्डिहाइड, ऐसीटोन (iii) बेन्जोइक अम्ल और एथिल बेन्जोएट के मध्य विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण दीजिए। (iv) एथेननाइट्राइल को ऐथेनैल में रूपांतरित करने के लिए अभिकर्मक का नाम लिखिए। (v) निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में 'X' की संरचना बनाइए : साइक्लोहेक्सेनॉल + CrO₃ → 'X'
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Answer the following questions : (i) Draw structure of the 2,4-dinitrophenyl hydrazone derivative of benzaldehyde. (ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN : Di-tert. butyl ketone, Acetaldehyde, Acetone (iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate. (iv) Write the name of the reagent to convert Ethanenitrile to Ethanal. (v) Draw the structure of 'X' in the following reaction : Cyclohexanol + CrO₃ → 'X'

key_points: (i) Structure: C₆H₅–CH=N–NH–C₆H₃(NO₂)₂ where the NO₂ groups are at positions 2 and 4 of the phenyl ring.
(ii) Increasing reactivity toward HCN: Di-tert. butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde. Steric hindrance decreases and +I effect of alkyl decreases in this order.

(iii) Add Na₂CO₃ / NaHCO₃ solution: benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence (CO₂ released), ethyl benzoate gives no effervescence. Or: add NaOH and heat (saponification) — ethyl benzoate hydrolyses to give ethanol (Lucas test); benzoic acid does not.
(iv) DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride) reduces ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) to ethanal (CH₃CHO) at low temperature.
(v) Cyclohexanol + CrO₃ → Cyclohexanone (the –OH is oxidised to C=O).

sub_questions.solution: For (i): The 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde is formed by the condensation of benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine. The structure is C₆H₅–CH=N–NH–C₆H₃(NO₂)₂ (with NO₂ at 2 and 4 positions). For (ii): Reactivity towards HCN depends on electrophilicity of carbonyl carbon and steric accessibility. More steric hindrance and more electron-donating alkyl groups reduce reactivity. Order: Di-tert. butyl ketone (most hindered) < Acetone (two CH₃, moderate) < Acetaldehyde (one CH₃ and one H, least hindered) — so increasing order is: Di-tert. butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde. For (iii): Add sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) solution — benzoic acid dissolves with brisk effervescence of CO₂ (acid stronger than H₂CO₃), while ethyl benzoate (an ester) does not react and gives no effervescence. For (iv): DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) at low temperature (–78°C) reduces ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) to ethanal (CH₃CHO) by partial reduction. For (v): Cyclohexanol (secondary alcohol) on treatment with CrO₃ (Jones' reagent) is oxidised to cyclohexanone. X = cyclohexanone (six-membered ring with C=O).

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक का उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: (a)(i) दिए गए E° मानों के आँकड़ों से, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए [E°M²⁺/M for V = –1.18, Cr = –0.91, Mn = –1.18, Fe = –0.44, Co = –0.28, Ni = –0.25, Cu = +0.34 V]: (I) उपरोक्त मानों में E°M²⁺/M अनियमित प्रवृत्ति क्यों दर्शाते हैं ? (II) E°Cu²⁺/Cu मान असाधारण धनात्मक क्यों है ? (III) E°Mn²⁺/Mn मान अत्यधिक ऋणात्मक क्यों है ? (a)(ii) पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट की अम्लीय और क्षारीय दोनों विलयनों में ऑक्सीकरण क्रिया के लिए I⁻ के साथ अभिक्रिया की आयनिक समीकरणें लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
(a)(i) From the given data of E° values, answer the following questions [E°M²⁺/M for V = –1.18, Cr = –0.91, Mn = –1.18, Fe = –0.44, Co = –0.28, Ni = –0.25, Cu = +0.34 V]: (I) Why E°M²⁺/M show irregular trend in the above values ? (II) Why is E°Cu²⁺/Cu value exceptionally positive ? (III) Why E°Mn²⁺/Mn value is highly negative ?
(a)(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with I⁻ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.

key_points: (I) Irregular trend because sublimation enthalpy, ionisation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy all vary irregularly across transition metals.
(II) E°Cu²⁺/Cu is exceptionally positive because Cu has high ionisation enthalpy and low heat of hydration compared to other transition metals; its 3d¹⁰ stable configuration is not easily disrupted.

(III) E°Mn²⁺/Mn is highly negative due to the extra stability of half-filled 3d⁵ configuration of Mn²⁺, making ionisation of Mn to Mn²⁺ relatively easy (low 2nd IE) but also the sublimation enthalpy and hydration factors make the overall process favour reduction less.
(ii) Acidic: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O; Alkaline: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻.

sub_questions.solution: For (i)(I): The standard electrode potentials E°M²⁺/M of transition metals show an irregular trend because the values depend on three competing factors — sublimation enthalpy (ΔsubH), sum of first and second ionisation enthalpies (IE₁ + IE₂), and hydration enthalpy (ΔhydH). These three quantities do not vary uniformly across the transition series, causing the E° values to be irregular. For (i)(II): E°Cu²⁺/Cu is exceptionally positive (+0.34 V) because copper has an unusually high sum of first and second ionisation enthalpies and a relatively low hydration enthalpy. The filled 3d¹⁰ sub-shell of Cu makes its electrons difficult to remove, and the low hydration enthalpy does not compensate, resulting in a less negative (positive) E° value. For (i)(III): E°Mn²⁺/Mn is highly negative (–1.18 V) because the Mn²⁺ ion has an exceptionally stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration (t2g³eg²), which gives extra stability through exchange energy. This extra stability of Mn²⁺ makes it difficult to reduce Mn²⁺ back to Mn, i.e., the reduction is not thermodynamically favourable, hence the highly negative value. For (ii): In acidic solution: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O. MnO₄⁻ is reduced to Mn²⁺ (gain of 5e⁻ each) and I⁻ is oxidised to I₂ (loss of 1e⁻ each). In alkaline solution: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻. MnO₄⁻ is reduced to MnO₂ and I⁻ is oxidised to IO₃⁻.

sub_questions.text: (b) निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए : (i) लैन्थेनॉयड श्रेणी के सदस्य का नाम लिखिए जो (I) +4 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था दर्शाता है और (II) +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था दर्शाता है। (ii) संक्रमण धातुएँ उत्तम उत्प्रेरक का कार्य क्यों करती हैं ? (iii) Mn की तुलना में Cr का गलनांक उच्च क्यों होता है ? (iv) क्या होता है जब पोटैशियम परमैंगनेट का अम्लीय विलयन कुछ समय के लिए रखा जाता है ? सम्बद्ध अभिक्रिया दीजिए। इस प्रकार की अभिक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Answer the following questions : (i) Name a member of the lanthanoid series which exhibits (I) +4 oxidation state (II) +2 oxidation state. (ii) Why transition metals act as good catalyst ? (iii) Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn ? (iv) What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime ? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called ?

key_points: (i)(I) Cerium (Ce) exhibits +4 oxidation state. (II) Europium (Eu) or Samarium (Sm) or Ytterbium (Yb) exhibit +2 oxidation state.
(ii) Transition metals have variable oxidation states and ability to form intermediate compounds; they also have large surface area as heterogeneous catalysts — both features help in catalysis.

(iii) Cr (3d⁵4s¹) has 6 unpaired electrons available for metallic bonding, giving it stronger metallic bonds and higher melting point. Mn (3d⁵4s²) has all d-orbitals half-filled with paired 4s — less effective metallic bonding.
(iv) Acidic KMnO₄ on standing undergoes auto-reduction (disproportionation): 4KMnO₄ + 2H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 4MnSO₄ + ... Actually: 4MnO₄⁻ + 4H⁺ → 4MnO₂ + 3O₂ + 2H₂O. This is called disproportionation.

sub_questions.solution: For (i): Lanthanoid with +4 oxidation state: Cerium (Ce, Z=58) — it readily forms Ce⁴⁺ due to the extra stability of the empty 4f⁰ configuration. Lanthanoid with +2 oxidation state: Europium (Eu, Z=63) or Ytterbium (Yb, Z=70) — Eu²⁺ has the stable half-filled 4f⁷ configuration and Yb²⁺ has the stable fully-filled 4f¹⁴ configuration. For (ii): Transition metals act as good catalysts because they have variable oxidation states (can form intermediate compounds with reactants) and provide an active surface for adsorption of reactants (heterogeneous catalysis), lowering the activation energy. The availability of d-orbitals for complex formation and electron transfer also facilitates catalytic cycles. For (iii): Chromium (Cr: [Ar]3d⁵4s¹) has 6 unpaired electrons (five 3d + one 4s) available for metallic bonding, leading to a stronger metallic lattice and higher melting point. Manganese (Mn: [Ar]3d⁵4s²) has a completely paired 4s² orbital reducing the effective metallic bonding, hence a lower melting point than Cr. For (iv): When acidic KMnO₄ solution is allowed to stand, it undergoes slow auto-reduction (self-reduction / disproportionation): 4MnO₄⁻ + 4H⁺ → 4MnO₂ + 3O₂ + 2H₂O. The MnO₄⁻ is partially reduced to MnO₂. This type of reaction is called disproportionation (auto-oxidation-reduction).

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: (a) 298 K पर निम्नलिखित सेल के लिए emf और ΔG परिकलित कीजिए : Mg(s) / Mg²⁺(0.01 M) // Ag⁺(0.001 M) / Ag(s). दिया है : E°Mg²⁺/Mg = –2.37 V, E°Ag⁺/Ag = +0.80 V. [1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹, log 10 = 1]
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Calculate emf and ΔG for the following cell at 298 K : Mg(s) / Mg²⁺(0.01 M) // Ag⁺(0.001 M) / Ag(s). Given : E°Mg²⁺/Mg = –2.37 V, E°Ag⁺/Ag = +0.80 V. [1 F = 96500 C mol–1, log 10 = 1]

key_points: Cell reaction: Mg + 2Ag⁺ → Mg²⁺ + 2Ag; n = 2.
E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = 0.80 – (–2.37) = 3.17 V.

sub_questions.solution: The cell is Mg(s)/Mg²⁺(0.01 M)//Ag⁺(0.001 M)/Ag(s). The cell reaction is: Mg(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s), with n = 2 electrons transferred. Standard cell EMF: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = (+0.80) – (–2.37) = 3.17 V. Reaction quotient: Q = [Mg²⁺]/[Ag⁺]² = 0.01/(0.001)² = 0.01/10⁻⁶ = 10⁴. Applying the Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q = 3.17 – (0.0591/2) × log 10⁴ = 3.17 – (0.02955 × 4) = 3.17 – 0.1182 = 3.0518 ≈ 3.05 V. Gibbs free energy: ΔG = –nFEcell = –2 × 96500 × 3.05 = –588650 J = –588.65 kJ.

sub_questions.text: (b) अभिक्रिया : 2AgCl(s) + H₂(g) (0.4 atm) → 2Ag(s) + 2H⁺(0.1 M) + 2Cl⁻(0.2 M). के लिए 25 °C पर सेल का emf परिकलित कीजिए। दिया है : ΔG° = –43500 J mol⁻¹. [log 10 = 1, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
sub_questions.text_english: (b) For the reaction : 2AgCl(s) + H₂(g) (0.4 atm) → 2Ag(s) + 2H⁺(0.1 M) + 2Cl⁻(0.2 M). Calculate emf of the cell at 25 °C. Given : ΔG° = –43500 J mol⁻¹. [log 10 = 1, 1 F = 96500 C mol–1]

key_points: n = 2 electrons (2AgCl + 2e⁻ → 2Ag + 2Cl⁻ at cathode; H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ at anode).

sub_questions.solution: The reaction 2AgCl(s) + H₂(g, 0.4 atm) → 2Ag(s) + 2H⁺(0.1 M) + 2Cl⁻(0.2 M) involves n = 2 electrons. Standard cell EMF from ΔG°: E°cell = –ΔG°/(nF) = –(–43500)/(2 × 96500) = 43500/193000 = 0.2254 V. Reaction quotient Q (pure solids and liquids omitted): Q = [H⁺]² × [Cl⁻]² / P(H₂) = (0.1)² × (0.2)² / 0.4 = 0.01 × 0.04 / 0.4 = 0.0004/0.4 = 0.001 = 10⁻³. Applying Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q = 0.2254 – (0.0591/2) × log(10⁻³) = 0.2254 – (0.02955) × (–3) = 0.2254 + 0.08865 = 0.3140 V ≈ 0.314 V.
